Something similar happened in Norway to a Czech family. Their two little boys were taken away from them a couple of years ago, and each was put into a different foster family, about 80 km apart. The biological parents are only allowed to visit the boys for something like 15 minutes once in 6 months; the mother isn't even allowed to hug them.

Recently Norway's version CPS (Barnevernet) decided to put one of the brothers up for adoption, and forbid the family from seeing the other boy completely as well. The family is trying to fight, but the organization that does this seems to stand completely above the law... and the kids have been taken away since 2011, so even if the family eventually manages to win, which won't happen any time soon, the Norse will just argue the same thing being argued here - the kids have spent so much time with other families that returning them isn't in their best interests.

It's not the first time this happened, either - there's an Indian family in a similar situation, and there was a Polish one, too. The Poles hired a private detective, and he in turn basically staged a "kidnapping" operation to get the kid back home.

Basically, he didn't need to spend money to create a new product, just copy and existing product and profit off of it. I wouldn't be able to sell it at my competitor's rates because I spent so much money on research and development.

The conclusion: it's not worth it to innovate. I just won't make new things. I'll just start taking other people's ideas and selling it for less.
